overview: The first fork in the road when a Gram-negative rod grows on MacConkey agar, and it changes the entire identification and treatment pathway.
genZNote: Sugar fermenters versus the gram-negatives that just won't.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A large order of Gram-negative rods (family Enterobacteriaceae and relatives) that ferment glucose, oxidase-negative, and typically found in the gut.
aspects.valueB: A diverse group of Gram-negative rods that do not ferment glucose oxidatively/fermentatively in the classic sense and are often oxidase-positive.

aspects.label: Glucose Fermentation
aspects.valueB: Utilizes glucose oxidatively or not at all — non-fermentative.

aspects.label: Oxidase Reaction
aspects.valueB: Frequently oxidase-positive (e.g. Pseudomonas), though not universal (e.g. Acinetobacter is oxidase-negative).

aspects.label: Representative Genera
aspects.valueA: Escherichia, Klebsiella, Proteus, Salmonella, Shigella, Enterobacter.

aspects.label: Natural Habitat
aspects.valueA: Predominantly gastrointestinal tract flora, some environmental.
aspects.valueB: Predominantly environmental (water, soil, moist hospital surfaces), with some human colonization.

aspects.label: Intrinsic Resistance Pattern
aspects.valueA: Generally more broadly antibiotic-susceptible at baseline, though acquired resistance is common.
aspects.valueB: Often intrinsically resistant to many antibiotic classes, making empiric therapy more limited from the start.

aspects.label: Clinical Context
aspects.valueA: Classic causes of UTIs, gut-associated infections, and community/hospital bacteremia.
aspects.valueB: Classic causes of hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia, especially in ICU settings.
